10.1: And Meleḵ Aḥashwĕrosh laid compulsory labor on the land and the islands of the sea.
10.2: And all the acts of his strength and his might, and the exact account of the greatness of Mordeḵai, with which the meleḵ made him great, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Maḏai and Paras?
10.3: For Mordeḵai the Yahuḏi was second to Meleḵ Aḥashwĕrosh, and great among the Yahuḏim and pleasing to his many brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.
10.4: Then Mordeḵai said, “Elohim has done these matters.
10.5: “For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters, and none of them have failed.
10.6: “A little fountain became a river, and there was light, and the sun, and much water. This river is Estĕr, whom the meleḵ married, and made Malkah.
10.7: “And the two dragons are Haman and I,
10.8: and the nations are those who were assembled to destroy the name of the Yahuḏim.
10.9: “And my nation is this Yisra’ĕl, which cried to Elohim, and were saved! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has saved His people, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has delivered us from all those evils, and Elohim has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the gentiles.
10.10: “Therefore He has made two lots: one for the people of Elohim, and another for all the gentiles.
10.11: “And these two lots came at the hour, and time, and day of judgment, before Elohim among all nations.”
10.12: So Elohim remembered His people, and rightly-ruled His inheritance.
10.13: Therefore those days shall be unto them in the month Aḏar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with an assembly, and joy, and with gladness before Elohim, according to their generations forever among His people.

11.1: In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemaeus and Cleopatra, Dositheos, who said he was a kohĕn and Lĕwite, and Ptolemaeus his son, brought this letter of Purim, which they said was the same, and that Lusimaḵos the son of Ptolemaeus, that was in Yerushalayim, had interpreted it.
11.2: In the second year of the reign of Artaḥshashta the great, on the first day of the month Nisan, Mordeḵai the son of Ya’ir, the son of Shim’i, the son of Qish, of the tribe of Binyamin, had a dream –
11.3: who was a Yahuḏi, and dwelt in the city of Shushan, a great man, being an attendant in the meleḵ’s court.
11.4: He was also one of the captives, which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the meleḵ of Baḇel carried from Yerushalayim with Yeḵonyah meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and this was his dream:
11.5: See, a noise of uproar, with thunder, and earthquakes, and disruption in the land!
11.6: And, see, two great dragons came forth ready to fight, and their cry was great.
11.7: And at their cry all nations were prepared for battle, that they might fight against the righteous people.
11.8: And see, a day of darkness and gloom, distress and anguish, affliction and great uproar upon the earth.
11.9: And the whole righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own evils, and were prepared to perish.
11.10: Then they cried to Elohim, and upon their cry, as it were from a little fountain, a great flood was made, even much water.
11.11: The light and the sun rose up, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the great.
11.12: Now when Mordeḵai, who had seen this dream, and what Elohim had determined to do, awoke, he regarded this dream in mind until night, and desired to know it by all means.

12.1: And Mordeḵai took his rest in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the meleḵ, and guards of the palace.
12.2: And he heard their schemes, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artaḥshashta the meleḵ; and so he informed the meleḵ of them.
12.3: Then the meleḵ examined the two eunuchs, and after they had confessed it, they were hanged.
12.4: And the meleḵ made a record of these matters, and Mordeḵai also wrote of them.
12.5: So the meleḵ commanded, Mordeḵai to serve in the court, and for this he rewarded him.
12.6: However, Haman the son of Hammeḏatha the Aḡaḡite, who was great in esteem with the meleḵ, sought to torture Mordeḵai and his people because of the two eunuchs of the meleḵ.

13.1: The copy of the letters was this: The great Meleḵ Artaḥshashta writes these matters to the princes and governors that are under him from Hodu to Kush in a hundred and twenty-seven provinces.
13.2: After I became ruler over many nations and reigned over the whole world, not lifted up with presumption of my authority, but carrying myself always with straightness and kindness, I purposed to settle my subjects continually in a quiet life, and make my reign peaceable, and open for passage to the farthest coasts, to renew peace, which is desired of all men.
13.3: Now when I asked my counsellors how this might be brought to pass, Haman, who excelled in wisdom among us, and was approved for his continual kindness and steadfast trustworthiness, and had the esteem of the second place in the reign,
13.4: declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had Laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commands of melaḵim, so that the uniting of our reigns, with esteem intended by us would not go forward.
13.5: Seeing therefore, we understand that these people alone are continually in opposition to all men, differing in the strange manner of their Laws, and evilly disposed toward our reign, working all the evil they may that our reign may not be firmly established;
13.6: therefore we have commanded that all those who are indicated in writing to you by Haman, who is appointed over the affairs, and is next to us, shall be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, with all their wives and children without any kindness or pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Aḏar of this present year.
13.7: That they, who of old and now also are malicious, shall in one day with violence go into the grave, and so, from now on cause our affairs to be well settled, and without trouble.
13.8: Then Mordeḵai thought upon all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and made his prayer to Him,
13.9: saying, “O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Meleḵ Almighty! For the whole world is in Your power, and if You have appointed to save Yisra’ĕl, there is none that disputes You.
13.10: “For You have made the shamayim and earth, and all the wonders under the shamayim.
13.11: You are Aḏon of all, and there is none that resists You, who is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
13.12: “You know all, and You know, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that it was neither in contempt nor pride, nor for any desire of esteem, that I did not bow down to proud Haman.
13.13: “For I could have been content for the deliverance of Yisra’ĕl to kiss the soles of his feet with kindness.
13.14: “But I did this, that I might not prefer the esteem of man above the esteem of Elohim; neither shall I worship any but You, O Elohim, neither shall I do it in pride.
13.15: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim and Meleḵ, spare Your people, for their eyes are upon us to bring us to naught! Indeed, they desire to destroy the inheritance, that has been Yours from the beginning.
13.16: “Do not despise the portion, which you have delivered out of Mitsrayim for Yourself.
13.17: “Hear my prayer, and be kind to Your inheritance. Turn our sorrow into joy, that we may live, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and praise Your Name, and do not destroy the mouths of those who praise you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
13.18: All Yisra’ĕl likewise cried most earnestly to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because their death was before their eyes.

14.1: Malkah Estĕr also, being in fear of death, came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
14.2: and laid aside her splendid apparel, and put on the garments of anguish and mourning. And instead of precious ointments, she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body greatly, and all the places of her joy she filled with her torn hair.
14.3: And she prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “O Aḏonai, You alone are our Meleḵ. Help me, an empty woman, who has no helper but You;
14.4: for my danger is at my hand!
14.5: “From my youth I have heard in the tribe of my family that You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, took Yisra’ĕl from among all people, and our fathers from all their forefathers, for an inheritance forever, and you have performed whatever You promised them.
14.6: “And now we have sinned before You. Therefore You have given us into the hands of our enemies,
14.7: because we worshipped their mighty ones. O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are righteous!
14.8: “Nevertheless it does not satisfy them that we are in bitter captivity; but they have vowed to their idols
14.9: that they shall abolish that which You have established with Your mouth, and destroy Your inheritance and stop the mouth of those who praise You, and quench the esteem of Your House and of Your altar.
14.10: “And open the mouths of the gentiles to give the praises to their idols, and to exalt a fleshly meleḵ forever.
14.11: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, do not give Your sceptre to those who are naught, and do not let them laugh at our fall; but turn their scheme upon themselves, and make an example of he who has begun this against us.
14.12: “Remember O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, make Yourself known in the time of our affliction, and give me boldness, O Meleḵ of the nations, and Aḏon of all power.
14.13: “Give me eloquent speech in my mouth before the lion; turn his heart to hate he who fights against us, that there may be an end of him and of all that are like-minded as him.
14.14: “But deliver us with Your hand, and help me, who is abandoned, and who has no other help but You.
14.15: “You know all, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; You know that I hate the esteem of the unrighteous, and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of all the gentiles.
14.16: “You know my need; for I abhor the sign of my high estate, which is upon my head in the days in which I show myself, and that I abhor it as a menstrual cloth, and that I do not wear it when I am alone by myself,
14.17: and that your female servant has not eaten at Haman’s table, and that I have not greatly esteemed the meleḵ’s feast, nor drunk the wine of the drink offerings.
14.18: Neither has Your female servant had any joy since the day that I was brought here to the present, but in You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Elohim of Aḇraham.
14.19: “You O mighty Elohim above all, hear the voice of the destitute and deliver us out of the hands of the evil-doers, and deliver me from my fear.

15.1: And on the third day, when she had ended her prayers, she put away her mourning garments, and put on her splendid apparel.
15.2: And being adorned in esteem, after she had called upon Elohim, who sees all and is Deliverer of all, she took two female servants with her,
15.3: and she leaned on the one, to carry herself daintily;
15.4: and the other followed, bearing up her train.
15.5: And she was tanned through the perfection of her beauty, and her countenance was cheerful and very delightful; but her heart was in anguish for fear.
15.6: Then having passed through all the doors, she stood before the meleḵ, who sat upon his royal throne, and was clothed with all his splendid robes, all glittering with gold and precious stones; and he was very frightening.
15.7: Then lifting up his face that shone with splendor, he looked very fiercely upon her. And the Malkah fell down, and went pale and fainted, and bowed herself upon the head of the female servant that went before her.
15.8: Then Elohim changed the spirit of the meleḵ into compassion, who in alarm leaped from his throne, and took her in his arms till she came to herself again, and comforted her with loving words and said to her,
15.9: “Estĕr, what is the matter? I am your brother, take courage.
15.10: “Though our law is established, you shall not die. Come near.”
15.11: And so he held up his golden sceptre, and laid it upon her neck,
15.12: and embraced her, and said, “Speak to me.”
15.13: Then she said to him, “I saw you, my master, as a messenger of Elohim, and my heart was troubled for fear of your greatness.
15.14: “For you are wondrous, master, and your face is full of favor.”
15.15: And as she was speaking, she fell down from faintness.
15.16: Then the meleḵ was troubled, and all his servants comforted her.

16.1: The great Meleḵ Artaḥshashta, to the princes and governors of a hundred and twenty-seven provinces from Hodu to Kush, and to all our trustworthy subjects, greetings:
16.2: For many, the more often they are esteemed with the great bounty of their esteemed princes, the prouder they have grown;
16.3: and do their best not only to harm our subjects, but not being able to handle wealth, also undertake to do against those who do good to them!
16.4: And not only take respect away from among men, but also lifted up with the esteemed words of wicked men that were never good, they think to escape the judgment of Elohim, who sees all and hates evil.
16.5: Also often flattering speech of those who are put in trust to manage the affairs of their friends, has caused many that are in authority to be partakers of innocent blood, and has surrounded them in incurable evils,
16.6: deceiving with the falsehood and deceit of their evil disposition the innocence and goodness of princes.
16.7: Now you may see this, as we have declared, not so much by ancient histories, as you may, if you search what has been done evilly of late through the corrupt behavior of those who are unworthily placed in authority.
16.8: And we must guard for the time to come, that our reign may be at rest and peaceable for all men,
16.9: both by changing our purposes, and always rightly ruling that which is evident with more equal proceeding.
16.10: For Haman, a Makedonian, the son of Hammeḏatha, being indeed a foreigner of Parasian blood, and far removed from our goodness, and as a foreigner received by us,
16.11: had obtained the favor that we show toward every nation so much, that he was called ‘our father,’ and was continually esteemed by all being the second to the meleḵ.
16.12: But he, not upholding his greatness, went about to deprive us of our reign and life;
16.13: having by many crafty deceits also sought from us the destruction of Mordeḵai, who saved our life, and continually worked for our good, as well as blameless Estĕr, a member of our reign, with their whole nation.
16.14: For by these means he thought, finding us lacking friends, to have the reign of Paras transferred to the Makedonians.
16.15: But we find that the Yahuḏim, whom this wicked wretch has delivered to utter destruction, are not evildoers, but live by most righteous Laws,
16.16: and that they are children of the Most High and Almighty, living Elohim, who has appointed the reign both to us and to our forefathers in the most excellent manner.
16.17: Therefore you shall do well not to put into action the letters sent to you by Haman the son of Hammeḏatha,
16.18: for he who was the worker of these matters, has been hanged at the gates of Shushan with all his family - Elohim, who rules over all, speedily rendering vengeance to him according to his deeds.
16.19: Therefore you shall publish the copy of this letter in all places, that the Yahuḏim may freely live after their own Laws.
16.20: And you shall aid them, even the same day, being the thirteenth day of the twelfth month Aḏar, that they may be avenged on those, who in the time of their affliction shall assault them.
16.21: For Ĕl Shaddai has turned the day to joy for them, in which the chosen people should have perished.
16.22: You shall therefore guard it a high day among your solemn Feasts with all feasting,
16.23: that both now and hereafter there may be safety for us and the highly respected of Paras. But to those who conspire against us - a remembrance of destruction.
16.24: Therefore every city and land whatever, which shall not do according to these matters, shall be destroyed without kindness with fire and sword, and shall be made not only impassable for men, but also greatly loathed by wild beasts and birds forever.
